newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end in retreat, down over one pct.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end in retreat, down over one pct.

text.p: French shares ended on Wednesday down more than one percent, taking their lead from a lower Wall Street to consolidate last week's substantial gains, traders said.

The market, which traded in negative ground all day, earlier tumbled after bond markets took fright on comments from the Bundesbank's chief economist Otmar Issing that there was no reason for further cuts in key interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 26.75 points or 1.23 percent at 2,148.86, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down seven at 2,152 from Tuesday's settle.
Volume was a brisk six billion francs
Food group Eridania Beghin-Say jumped 1.77 percent to 803 francs on prospects of cheaper raw materials.
The stock also benefited from a presentation from rival Saint-Louis to analysts this morning which pointed to promising prospects for the food ingredients sector.
Insurer Gan ends off lows, down 0.82 percent at 120.50 francs, after reporting first-half net loss of nearly one billion francs.
Holiday resorts group Club Mediterannee dives 17.34 percent to 329 francs after Tuesday's profit warning. The share fall prompts Paribas to put a sell note on hotelier Accor.
